comparisons.relationship: NASA documents a Haughton–Shackleton analogy at whole-crater and operations levels; this record narrows the field comparison to Locale 7 and one Shackleton rim image.

terrain.evidence: Locale 7 has a rocky ridge, lower shelf and boulders that complicated rover access. The Shackleton rim detail shows blocks, small craters and impact-related surface textures.
terrain.difference: The sources do not establish matching slopes, block distributions or a safe lunar route. Haughton is a modified complex impact structure; Shackleton is a well-preserved simple crater.

geology.evidence: Locale 7 investigated carbonate host-rock layers and blocks. The lunar rim map describes upper regolith; the blocks are interpreted as likely ejecta, without measured composition in that source.
geology.difference: The documented carbonate host rock differs materially from the lunar regolith and ejecta interpretation.

practice.label: Impact-landform observation
practice.reason: Both sources support interpreting impact-related terrain from mapped features.

practice.label: Robotic mapping and traverse planning
practice.reason: NASA tested field mapping and rover access at Site A; LROC prepared the lunar map for traverse planning.

limits: Earth erosion, glaciation, permafrost and carbonates differ from lunar regolith.
Lunar vacuum, gravity, radiation and polar lighting are not reproduced at Haughton.
No landing-site, route-safety or permanent-base suitability follows from this review.

comparisons.reviewNotes: Source-based desk screening; figure locators, not equal-area polygons or measured terrain metrics.

comparisons.relationship: The specific Copper Canyon–Peace Vallis pairing is TerraTwin's proposal. Published sources document each named fan, but no completed pair review is recorded.

terrain.evidence: USGS describes Copper Canyon's radial drainage. Palucis et al. map Peace Vallis upper and lower fan units and channels.
terrain.difference: The whole fans are about 5.2 km² and 80 km² respectively; matching feature scales and preservation have not been assessed.
terrain.missingReason: Terrain evidence has not been reviewed together under the P07 rubric.

geology.evidence: USGS describes Copper Canyon sediment sources; Palucis et al. describe Peace Vallis fan deposits.
geology.difference: Corresponding deposit classes and material uncertainty have not been reviewed at selected units.
geology.missingReason: Geology evidence has not been reviewed together under the P07 rubric.

limits: The named-fan analogy is proposed, not a published assessment of these two fans together.
Current Martian conditions differ from terrestrial rainfall and sediment transport.
Copper Canyon public access is restricted; do not treat this candidate as an approved field site (NPS S28).
No traversability or base suitability claim follows from this candidate.
